claims.summary: Cynthia strikes a bargain with Mephisto for magical power.
claims.qualification: Agreement does not mean informed acceptance of the ultimate cost.
claims.scope: Doctor Strange & Doctor Doom: Triumph and Torment (1989)

claims.summary: Mephisto takes Cynthia’s soul following the bargain.
claims.qualification: Power asymmetry; precise contractual terms not panel-verified.
claims.scope: Doctor Strange & Doctor Doom: Triumph and Torment (1989)

claims.summary: Marvel identifies Cynthia as Victor’s mother.
claims.qualification: Kinship does not establish agreement with his later rule.

claims.summary: Doom rescues Cynthia’s soul from Mephisto.
claims.qualification: One rescue does not erase the effects of Doom’s other actions.

claims.summary: Strange helps Doom free Cynthia’s soul.
claims.qualification: No independent personal friendship with Cynthia is established.

claims.summary: Kristoff is identified as Doom’s adopted heir.
claims.qualification: Some later solicitations call him a son; biological paternity not established.

claims.summary: Doom kidnaps Kristoff while he is seeking legal relief.
claims.qualification: A specific 2014 incident, not a perpetual state.

claims.summary: Doom tasks Kristoff with creating the Superior Avengers.
claims.qualification: 2025 institutional assignment; not proof of affectionate trust.

claims.summary: Jennifer accepts Kristoff’s extradition-related legal matter.
claims.qualification: Attorney-client relationship; private friendship not inferred.

claims.summary: Jennifer pursues Kristoff’s release in Latveria.
claims.qualification: Professional duty and protective action can coexist.

claims.summary: Jennifer undertakes an international jailbreak to recover Doom’s captive.
claims.qualification: Event-scoped opposition; exact combat choreography unverified.

claims.summary: Zorba leads resistance against Doom’s rule.
claims.qualification: Claim of legitimacy does not prove later benevolence.

claims.summary: Doom retakes Latveria from Zorba, who is described as seemingly killed.
claims.qualification: Do not claim a confirmed permanent death.

claims.summary: Zorba and the Fantastic Four act together to depose Doom.
claims.qualification: Reed-specific dialogue and intentions not established; group-action evidence.

claims.summary: Doom publicly names Victorious his intended bride and devoted subject.
claims.qualification: No completed marriage or reciprocated love established.

claims.summary: Victorious is presented as Doom’s devoted subject and intended bride.
claims.qualification: Publisher language may reflect Latverian propaganda; consent not panel-verified.

claims.summary: Fury launches an unsanctioned mission against von Bardas.
claims.qualification: Political conflict is documented; not a claim about personal hatred.

claims.summary: Von Bardas retaliates for Fury’s attack with a supervillain assault.
claims.qualification: Retaliation targets multiple heroes; exact personal confrontation unverified.

claims.summary: Scorcher is said to be forced into her bomb-linked attack.
claims.qualification: Unverified Marvel-hosted crowd-sourced account; provisional.

claims.summary: Daisy Johnson overcomes von Bardas.
claims.qualification: Publisher Fury biography confirms defeat; precise lethality disputed/unchecked.

claims.summary: Scorcher reportedly accepts a contract on Matt and later battles Daredevil.
claims.qualification: Unverified crowd-sourced biography; original issues pending.

claims.summary: Marvel identifies the murdered Valeria as Doom’s former love.
claims.qualification: Historical romance, not evidence of affection at time of killing.

claims.summary: Doom murders Valeria to obtain mystical power.
claims.qualification: Lethal instrumental act, not reciprocal rivalry.

identity_warnings: Cynthia von Doom is Victor’s mother; Valeria the former lover is distinct from the child Valeria Richards (canonical id valeria).
Kristoff is identified as an adopted heir in Marvel history; the biological son wording in solicitations is not proof of paternity.
Victorious is Zora Vukovic; civilian name crosschecked outside publisher, publisher wedding source names only Victorious.
Prince Zorba’s apparent death is not a verified permanent death.
Scorcher’s Marvel-hosted biography carries an explicit crowd-sourced unverified notice; related claims remain provisional.
Daisy overcomes Lucia von Bardas; do not overclaim her final death or exact mechanism.
No Zora–Johnny Storm pair included: two official-source searches did not yield sufficient issue-level publisher evidence.
The canonical pilot does not include Jennifer Walters, although the broader Earth-616 atlas does.
